Synopsis

The astroonauta npm account takeover also compromised react-native-country-select, a direct dependency of react-native-international-phone-number.

Story

The first react-native-country-select payload was small at the package boundary and large after execution. Version 0.3.91 added a preinstall hook that ran node install.js before npm finished the install. Aikido found the adjacent 0.3.9 release clean, making the change narrow and easy to describe: one new loader file and one lifecycle hook.

The loader reached to Solana RPC, recovered a transaction memo, decoded a URL, and fetched a second stage. The recovered chain continued through AES-decrypted JavaScript and a Google Calendar URL used as another indirection point before fetching more content from attacker infrastructure. The same install.js loader hash appeared in both React Native packages compromised that morning.

The later payload was Windows-focused theft code, not a harmless beacon. It set persistence with schtasks and an HKCU Run key, wrote an init.json guard, downloaded Node.js runtimes into AppData, walked browser profile and wallet storage, killed browser processes, stole npm and GitHub credentials, and exfiltrated collected archives. StepSecurity later tracked the attacker returning with additional releases that hid delivery behind transitive dependencies.
